chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from al-Hasan ibn Sadah, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and said: 'Some of our companions have narrated that it is permissible for a man to marry the slave-girl of his son and the slave-girl of his daughter. And I have a daughter and a son, and for my daughter I bought a slave-girl from her dowry. So is it permissible for me to have intercourse with her?' He said: 'No, except with her permission.'
Al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm said: 'Is it not that this has come as permissible?' He said: 'Yes, that is if he himself is the cause (of her acquisition).

Then he turned to me and pointed towards me with his index finger and said: 'When you buy for your daughter a slave-girl or for your son, and the son is young and has not had intercourse with her, it is permissible for you to take possession of her and marry her. Otherwise, it is not permissible except with their permission.'
ai.seo_question: Can a father marry the slave-girl he bought for his young son?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the fiqh of 'tamalluk' (ownership) regarding a father's right to marry the slave-girls of his children, distinguishing between cases where the father purchased the slave-girl for a minor son who has not yet consummated the marriage versus other scenarios. He emphasizes that while ownership may grant the right to marry, the consent of the slave-girl remains a prerequisite, and if the son is an adult or has consummated the marriage, his permission is also required. This ruling highlights the nuanced Shia jurisprudence on the intersection of paternal authority, property rights, and individual consent within the family structure.
